key_insight: The paper proves a general connectivity-based upper bound on the dimension of simple GHZ graphs, showing that higher vertex connectivity still limits, but does not eliminate, the possible GHZ-state dimension.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum-optics and quantum-network designers a graph-theoretic criterion for estimating when a photonic setup can or cannot realize high-dimensional multipartite GHZ states.
method: Derive a bound on GHZ-graph dimension using vertex connectivity κ(G).
Extend the analysis to bounds based on edge connectivity and maximum degree.
Compare against prior results on low-connectivity graphs and the Krenn–Gu–Zeilinger conjecture.
evidence_signal: The abstract states a proved theorem: for every simple connected GHZ graph with at least four vertices, the dimension is at most 2^{κ(G)-1}+C(κ(G),2), with additional bounds for edge connectivity and maximum degree.
watch_item: The bound is theoretical and graph-structural, so translating it into an experimental photonic design still requires verifying that a proposed setup matches the GHZ-graph assumptions.
